# Background

This repository reproduces the comparison analysis testing whether the
negative association between **homologous recombination (HR)** rate and
**prophage density**, reported across 23 bacterial taxa by
[Kwun & Croucher (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1093/ismejo/wrag256), can explain
the large-scale pangenome structure variation described across the bacterial
domain by
[Horsfield *et al.*](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.02.04.703695)
(*Pansim*/*PopPUNK-mod*).

No pre-merged CSV is stored in this repository. Instead, all merging is
performed live from **three raw, unmodified source files** in
`data/raw/` by `R/data_prep.R::build_analysis_datasets()`:

- `supplementary_file1_408species.csv` — Horsfield *et al.*'s
  **Supplementary File 1**: PopPUNK-mod pangenome-dynamics parameters and
  pangenome composition statistics for 408 bacterial species (one row per
  species).
- `supplementary_file8_negexp_fits.csv` — Horsfield *et al.*'s
  **Supplementary File 8**: negative-exponential core-vs-accessory pairwise
  distance curve fits (Plateau, Rate ratio, Y-intercept; their Equation 1)
  for 22 species/datasets, in long format.
- `recombination_conflict_comparison_plot.csv` — Kwun & Croucher's own
  per-taxon output (n = 23 taxa) giving the geNomad Caudoviricetes
  prophage density (`lambda_hat`, Poisson MLE + 95% CI) and the
  probability of diversification through homologous recombination
  (`Recombination probability`, from their MLST-based beta-binomial GLMM +
  asymptotic CI), together with `Transformability` and `Niche`
  annotations, produced directly by their
  [recombination-conflict](https://github.com/nickjcroucher/recombination-conflict)
  pipeline.

`build_analysis_datasets()` joins these three files together, taking
species-level means across constituent species for genus-level ("spp.")
taxa, and matching *Enterococcus faecium* to the GTDB-style label
`Enterococcus_B faecium` used in Supplementary File 1 (see
`data/README.md` for full details of the matching logic).

```{r load-data}
datasets <- build_analysis_datasets(
  file1_path = "data/raw/supplementary_file1_408species.csv",
  file8_path = "data/raw/supplementary_file8_negexp_fits.csv",
  plot_path  = "data/raw/recombination_conflict_comparison_plot.csv"
)

main_df   <- datasets$main_df
negexp_df <- datasets$negexp_df
```

## Taxa included

`main_df` contains all 23 taxa for which Kwun & Croucher estimated both
prophage density and HR probability, each joined to its corresponding
Horsfield *et al.* pangenome-dynamics parameters. `n_species_matched`
records how many Supplementary File 1 species rows contributed to each
taxon's values (> 1 for the genus-level "spp." taxa, which are
unweighted means across their constituent species).

```{r taxa-table}
main_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Species = display %>%
      stringr::str_replace("italic\\('([^']+)'\\)~'spp\\.'", "\\1 spp.") %>%
      stringr::str_replace("italic\\('([^']+)'\\)", "\\1")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Species, Transformability, Niche,
               lambda_hat, `Recombination probability`, n_species_matched) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Species) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    `Prophage density (lambda_hat)` = lambda_hat,
    `HR probability` = `Recombination probability`,
    `Species averaged (Supp. File 1)` = n_species_matched
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = FALSE)
```

A further 8 of the 23 taxa (*Bacillus subtilis*, *Citrobacter* spp.,
*Enterobacter* spp., *Enterococcus faecium*, *Morganella morganii*,
*Proteus* spp., *Serratia* spp. and *Vibrio cholerae*) have no
corresponding entry in Horsfield *et al.*'s Supplementary File 8 and are
therefore absent from `negexp_df` (n = 15), used in the Y-intercept
analysis below.

# Pangenome size tracks prophage density, not HR

```{r pan-genes-vs-lambda, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
pan_vs_lambda <- plot_correlation(
  main_df,
  x_var = "lambda_hat", y_var = "pan_genes",
  x_lab = "Expected number of prophage per isolate (lambda_hat)",
  y_lab = "Pangenome size (pan_genes)"
)
pan_vs_lambda$plot
```
*`r pan_vs_lambda$caption_note`*

```{r rare-genes-vs-lambda, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
rare_vs_lambda <- plot_correlation(
  main_df,
  x_var = "lambda_hat", y_var = "rare_genes",
  x_lab = "Expected number of prophage per isolate (lambda_hat)",
  y_lab = "Number of rare accessory genes"
)
rare_vs_lambda$plot
```
*`r rare_vs_lambda$caption_note`*

By contrast, HR probability is weakly *negatively* associated with
pangenome size — the opposite of what would be expected if HR itself
inflated the pangenome:

```{r pan-genes-vs-HR, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
pan_vs_hr <- plot_correlation(
  main_df,
  x_var = "Recombination probability", y_var = "pan_genes",
  x_lab = "Probability of diversification through HR",
  y_lab = "Pangenome size (pan_genes)"
)
pan_vs_hr$plot
```
*`r pan_vs_hr$caption_note`*

# The proportion of rapidly-exchanged genes and basal turnover rate are best explained by HR

```{r propfast-vs-HR, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
propfast_vs_hr <- plot_correlation(
  main_df,
  x_var = "Recombination probability", y_var = "prop_genes2_median",
  x_lab = "Probability of diversification through HR",
  y_lab = "Proportion of rapidly-exchanged ('fast') genes"
)
propfast_vs_hr$plot
```
*`r propfast_vs_hr$caption_note`*

`rate_genes1_median`'s 95% credible interval is extremely wide for a small
number of taxa (most notably *Haemophilus influenzae* and *Neisseria* spp.),
which otherwise stretches the vertical axis so far that the bulk of the
points become compressed into a narrow band at the bottom of the plot. The
axis below is therefore truncated (zoomed in on the bulk of the data) to
emphasise the individual points and their error bars; the regression line
and the reported *r*, *R*<sup>2</sup> and *p* are still fitted to the full,
untruncated data (see caption).

```{r baseturnover-vs-HR, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
baseturnover_vs_hr <- plot_correlation(
  main_df,
  x_var = "Recombination probability", y_var = "rate_genes1_median",
  x_lab = "Probability of diversification through HR",
  y_lab = "Basal gene turnover rate",
  ylim = c(0, 0.0025)
)
baseturnover_vs_hr$plot
```
*`r baseturnover_vs_hr$caption_note`*

# Core mutation rate is only weakly, and non-robustly, related to HR

```{r coremu-vs-HR, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
coremu_vs_hr <- plot_correlation(
  main_df,
  x_var = "Recombination probability", y_var = "core_mu_median",
  x_lab = "Probability of diversification through HR",
  y_lab = "Core mutation rate"
)
coremu_vs_hr$plot
```
*`r coremu_vs_hr$caption_note`*

# Genome-size-scaled Y-intercept of the core/accessory distance curve tracks prophage density

Multiplying the fitted Y-intercept (instantaneous gene turnover rate) from
the negative-exponential core-vs-accessory distance regression by genome
size gives a substantially stronger relationship with `lambda_hat` than the
raw Y-intercept alone (see analysis notes in `README.md`).

```{r yintercept-vs-lambda, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
yint_vs_lambda <- plot_correlation(
  negexp_df,
  x_var = "lambda_hat", y_var = "Y-intercept x genome size",
  x_lab = "Expected number of prophage per isolate (lambda_hat)",
  y_lab = "Y-intercept x genome size"
)
yint_vs_lambda$plot
```
*`r yint_vs_lambda$caption_note`* The negative-exponential curve fit
(`Plateau (i)`, `Rate ratio (k)`, `Y-intercept (j)`) was reported by
Horsfield *et al.* as point estimates only, with no confidence intervals
available in the source supplementary data, so horizontal error bars for
`lambda_hat` are shown but vertical error bars for the derived
`Y-intercept x genome size` quantity cannot be added without fabricating
uncertainty that was not reported.

# Naturally transformable taxa have smaller pangenomes, but this tracks their lower prophage burden

```{r transformability-pangenome, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6}
transformability_pangenome <- plot_violin_comparison(
  main_df,
  x_var = "Transformability", y_var = "pan_genes",
  x_lab = "Transformability", y_lab = "Pangenome size (pan_genes)"
)
transformability_pangenome$plot
```
*Each point is one taxon's `pan_genes` value (no reported per-taxon
uncertainty interval); the violin shows the full distribution within each
group and the annotated Wilcoxon rank-sum test quantifies the uncertainty
in the group-level comparison, so no additional per-point error bars are
drawn here, consistent with `plot_violin_kw()` in the source repository.*

```{r transformability-vs-lambda-joint, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
# Do transformable and non-transformable taxa fall on the same lambda_hat
# relationship, or are they offset once prophage density is accounted for?
joint_model <- lm(pan_genes ~ lambda_hat + Transformability, data = main_df)
broom::tidy(joint_model) %>%
  kableExtra::kbl(digits = 3, caption = "Joint model: pan_genes ~ lambda_hat + Transformability") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = FALSE)

ggplot(main_df, aes(x = lambda_hat, y = pan_genes)) +
  # Single overall trend line (group = 1 prevents this from being split by
  # the colour/shape mapped on the point/error-bar layers below)
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), method = "lm", se = FALSE,
             colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lambda_lwr, xmax = lambda_upr, colour = Transformability),
                height = 0, alpha = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = Transformability, shape = Niche), size = 2.5) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(aes(label = display), parse = TRUE, size = 3,
                            show.legend = FALSE, max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = niche_palette) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = transformability_palette) +
  labs(x = "Expected number of prophage per isolate (lambda_hat)",
      y = "Pangenome size (pan_genes)") +
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(title.position = "top", nrow = 1),
    shape  = guide_legend(title.position = "top")
  ) +
  theme_conflict()
```
*Horizontal error bars show the 95% CI on `lambda_hat` (Poisson MLE).
`pan_genes` has no reported uncertainty interval in the source data, so no
vertical error bars are shown.*

Once `lambda_hat` is included in the model, `Transformability` adds no
additional explanatory power (see coefficient table above): transformable
and non-transformable taxa fall along the *same* `lambda_hat` regression
line rather than forming offset clusters, indicating that the smaller
pangenomes of transformable taxa are explained by their lower prophage
burden rather than by transformability / HR directly.

# Combined summary figure

```{r combined-figure, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 11}
combine_with_legend(
  list(
    pan_vs_lambda$plot   + ggtitle("A"),
    propfast_vs_hr$plot  + ggtitle("B"),
    yint_vs_lambda$plot  + ggtitle("C"),
    transformability_pangenome$plot + ggtitle("D")
  ),
  labels = NULL, nrow = 2, ncol = 2, legend_source = 1
)
```

# Summary of correlation statistics

```{r summary-table}
tribble(
  ~Relationship, ~r, ~R2, ~p,
  "pan_genes ~ lambda_hat",                 pan_vs_lambda$r,        pan_vs_lambda$r2,        pan_vs_lambda$p_value,
  "rare_genes ~ lambda_hat",                rare_vs_lambda$r,       rare_vs_lambda$r2,       rare_vs_lambda$p_value,
  "pan_genes ~ Recombination probability",  pan_vs_hr$r,            pan_vs_hr$r2,            pan_vs_hr$p_value,
  "prop_genes2_median ~ Recombination probability", propfast_vs_hr$r, propfast_vs_hr$r2,     propfast_vs_hr$p_value,
  "rate_genes1_median ~ Recombination probability", baseturnover_vs_hr$r, baseturnover_vs_hr$r2, baseturnover_vs_hr$p_value,
  "core_mu_median ~ Recombination probability",     coremu_vs_hr$r, coremu_vs_hr$r2,         coremu_vs_hr$p_value,
  "(Y-intercept x genome size) ~ lambda_hat",       yint_vs_lambda$r, yint_vs_lambda$r2,     yint_vs_lambda$p_value
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(across(c(r, R2, p), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>%
  knitr::kable() %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = FALSE)
```
